lesson.title: Research symposium: defend, review and close the evidence loop
lesson.short: Questions · peer review · limits · research synthesis
lesson.timeMeaning: Suggested independent study minutes; not scheduled contact time
lesson.lead: A good answer in discussion separates what the experiment establishes from what would require another experiment.
goals: Answer critical questions with evidence and calibrated uncertainty.
Give actionable peer feedback without inventing a grading scheme.
Identify the next experiment and preserve the final artifact.

sections.title: Start here: prerequisites and course status
sections.html:
An audience asks whether a one-GPU result doubles on two GPUs. The honest answer depends on evidence already collected, not confidence in the speaker. This lesson practices answering precisely, reviewing another group's claim and preserving what the discussion changes.

Bring the claim, limits and artifact path from lesson 36. Questions and review forms are original practice suggestions. This supplemental session is not an Edinburgh lecture or verified Canvas assignment; grading weights, deadlines, upload destinations and mandatory formats remain unverified.

sections.title: Prepare for four kinds of questions
sections.html:
Listen to the full question, then identify what it challenges. A meaning question asks the scope: workload, metric and operating condition. A fairness question asks whether quality, resources and tuning were comparable. A mechanism question asks what ablation supports the explanation. A generality question asks about a different scale, skew, concurrency, drift or hardware.

Answer the narrow point first and point to the relevant protocol or trace. Do not substitute a favorable number from another condition. If a question exposes a flaw, name its effect on the conclusion. If evidence is missing, say what is unmeasured and which experiment would resolve it.

For a theory claim, this may mean restating assumptions and a counterexample outside them. For a system claim, it may mean showing the timing boundary or failure count. Both are stronger than improvising a result that was never run.

Key takeaway

“We have not measured that” is a useful scientific answer when followed by the experiment that would resolve it.

sections.title: Worked discussion: three strong responses
sections.html:
Question: “Would two H100s double throughput?” If only one was measured, say that. Routing, placement and communication remain unmeasured. If both were measured, give the actual ratio under matched workload and quality with overheads; device count does not derive speedup.

Question: “The median improves; what about slow requests?” If tails/failures were collected, show p95/p99 and timeout breakdown, including regressing subgroups. If not, the median cannot supply their behavior: state that limitation and propose a timeout-aware tail test.

Question: “Does your LLM evaluator prove correctness?” Agreement alone measures agreement. Explain the independent held-out human/factual check only if it actually happened, with its guide and sample. Shared evaluator errors remain possible.

Why is “not measured yet” an incomplete but useful answer?

It protects the boundary of the current evidence. Complete it with a test: match recall and workload, run one/two devices, include routing and merge time, and report failures. Now the uncertainty has an actionable resolution.

sections.title: Peer review that helps another group improve
sections.html:
Begin peer review by restating the group's central claim in your own words. Record its strongest evidence, one unclear assumption, an alternative explanation and one discriminating test or presentation change. Add a course connection that helps them reason, not just a score.

For example, replace “bad ANN benchmark” with “the two QPS points have different recall, so this graph does not isolate speed at equal quality.” Ask whether matched-quality sweeps exist. That is a testable methodological concern. If the sweep exists but the slide omits it, the issue is missing explanation instead.

Theory review asks assumptions, statement, proof idea and counterexamples. Systems review asks correctness, resources, workload and comparison. Neither is assessed solely by a speed chart. This discussion form is suggested practice, not an official rubric.

A carefully controlled study reports no gain. What useful feedback remains?

Check whether the hypothesis was meaningful and tests ruled out plausible benefits under the stated conditions. Suggest the experiment most likely to distinguish the remaining explanations. Do not require a positive speedup to recognize a supported finding.

sections.title: Synthesize the frontier themes with the core course
sections.html:
Connect the frontier topics to familiar responsibilities. Learned cardinalities change selectivity and plan decisions. Vector search changes how an index trades work for approximation. Semantic pipelines revisit operator order but must define permitted label error. Disaggregation moves buffers, logging and ownership across layers.

Ask the same question in each: which contract is preserved while cost falls? Exact relational operators may require equivalent SQL results. ANN needs a quality target within an eligible set. Semantic operators need a reference or labeling policy. Recovery needs durability and permitted histories.

Then locate the optimized layer and the claimed benefit. A faster kernel can leave application latency unchanged. Better average estimates can still produce harmful threshold decisions. Faster steady-state access can coexist with worse restart behavior. Use one trace from your project to explain that gap rather than claiming every layer inherits the improvement.

sections.title: Close the project with an evidence handoff
sections.html:
After discussion, preserve final code/configuration, input instructions, raw outputs, report/slides and an errata or open-question note. Record factual corrections and revise unsupported wording. Follow the instructor's actual submission and sharing process; this companion specifies no deadline, upload location or marking weight.

Choose the next test by how much it could change your belief. A small counterexample separating queueing from device work may be more informative than a larger version of the same benchmark. State which explanations it distinguishes.

A figure labeled milliseconds as seconds. What must be corrected?

Check the raw data, fix the axis and every derived claim, preserve an explanation of the correction and inform the relevant audience through the actual course process. Check neighboring figures too; do not assume the error is isolated.

The final handoff should let another reader see what is supported, what changed during discussion and exactly how to run the next check.

Key takeaway

Finish with a trustworthy answer and a reproducible path to the next question.

questions.question: How should peer feedback distinguish missing explanation from a methodological flaw?
options: Treat both as proof of bad intent.
Assign a grading weight invented by the reviewer.
Ignore all uncertainty.
Ask for clarification and identify the specific evidence or control that is missing.
questions.explanation: Actionable scientific feedback is specific and evidence-based; the official assessment scheme is separate.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: What does improved median latency establish about p99?
options: Nothing by itself; tail behavior needs its own evidence.
Tail latency is irrelevant in every workload.
P99 is always the same as the maximum.
P99 must improve equally.
questions.explanation: A median summarizes the middle observation; it does not characterize rare slow requests or failures.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: A unit error is found in a final figure. What should the group do?
options: Correct it, check derived claims and communicate the correction through the appropriate course process.
Leave it unchanged because the talk is over.
Change only the title, regardless of data.
Delete the raw results.
questions.explanation: An evidence handoff includes factual corrections and preserves traceability. Unit errors can affect interpretation and derived claims.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: What is the most informative next experiment after a symposium?
options: A test that could resolve the most important remaining confound or uncertainty.
A rerun selected only to produce a positive result.
The largest possible run regardless of question.
A different chart color.
questions.explanation: Choose the experiment by how much it could change the scientific conclusion, not merely by scale.
